newsitem.title: USA: Delta pilots seek wage increase.
newsitem.headline: Delta pilots seek wage increase.

text.p: The pilots of Delta Air Lines Inc said they will seek pay raises and work rule changes only one year after ratifying the current four-year contract.

Citing Delta's record third quarter profits and recent pay raises for non-union employees, the pilots said "recent events at both our company and in our industry raise serious questions about the fairness and equity of maintaining the status quo."
The pilots did not provide specific wage goals or work rule changes.

Delta's pilots ratified a four-year contract in April 1996. Its provisions included a two percent pay reduction in return for stock options, a profit-sharing plan comparable to those enjoyed by other Delta employees, a seat on the company's board and improved retirement benefits.
At the time, Delta said it expected to save in excess of $750 million over the four years as a result of the collective bargaining agreement reached with the pilots.
Delta's pilots now contend that the situation at the nation's third largest airline has changed.

"When we entered into our contract a year ago, the pilots made a collective decision to accept major changes to our working agreement in an effort to assist...in making Delta more competitive and to return the company to sustained profitability," the union's master executive council said in a recorded message to the pilots.

"Delta management has now consciously altered both their revenue and cost cutting goals and has announced a much-deserved pay raise for non-contract employees. Against this backdrop, it is time to reconsider the pilots' level of participation needed to accomplish management's now-modified goals," the union said.

The Delta pilots also said there is a "growing disparity between Delta's pilot compensation and the compensation of our peers in the industry -- a disparity that will significantly increase over the next few years."

Pilots at AMR Corp American Airlines recently ratified a five-year labor contract that offered a nine percent wage increase. Pilots at UAL Corp's United Airlines also approved a proposal that includes two mid-term wage increases of five percent.

Analysts said the efforts by Delta's pilots to secure a wage increase may be clouded by the pending retirement of Delta's chief executive and chairman Ronald Allen, which was announced separately on Monday.
